headline.text: Keski-Pohjanmaa's crude multidisciplinary team recording share of 1.4% (95% CI 0.4–4.8; n=2/148) is below the 6.0% (893/14873) national value, though this measures recording practice rather than care.

details.text: In Keski-Pohjanmaa, a multidisciplinary team meeting is recorded for a crude share of 1.4% (95% CI 0.4–4.8; n=2/148) compared with 6.0% (893/14873) nationally, with the 95% confidence interval excluding the national value, though these records measure recording practice rather than care because HILMO captures procedures only from direct patient contacts.

Because treatment categories overlap, Keski-Pohjanmaa's crude shares are 22.3% (95% CI 16.3–29.7; n=33/148) versus 27.0% (4009/14873) nationally for curative, 32.4% (95% CI 25.4–40.3; n=48/148) versus 30.4% (4522/14873) for life-prolonging, and 46.6% (95% CI 38.8–54.6; n=69/148) versus 39.5% (5871/14873) for symptomatic treatment, with each 95% confidence interval including the national value.

A crude share of 25.0% (95% CI 18.7–32.5; n=37/148) in Keski-Pohjanmaa has no treatment record within 12 months compared with 27.5% (4089/14873) nationally, where the 95% confidence interval includes the national value and the category mixes untreated patients with unrecorded treatment.

In preliminary, unpublished national figures for Finland, the pathway from symptoms to treatment averages 155 days—with 56 days of patient delay, 41 days in primary care, and 58 days in specialist care—compared with 107 days in Sweden and 67 days in Denmark.

headline.text: Public registry data lack stage at diagnosis for about 48% of patients and do not capture primary care visits, referral dates, or treatment start times.

details.text: County figures, like the crude 22.3% (95% CI 16.3–29.7; n=33/148) curative share versus 27.0% (4009/14873) nationally, are not age-adjusted—age-adjusted values exist only from Kuva 16 for curative treatment by sex, with digitised national lines of 26.7% for men and 26.9% for women at ±0.5 percentage points—and separately cannot be stage-adjusted with stage missing for about 48% of patients.

A journal article found that HILMO hospital discharge diagnoses match the Cancer Registry for about 90% of most cancer types, whereas lung cancer data reporting, collection, and storage are currently incomplete and Finland has no cancer quality registry.

Public report data do not measure symptoms, referral dates, specialist visit timing, or treatment start dates; primary care visits are not included in the report's data, occupational health is not mentioned at all, and imaging appears only indirectly as the clinical basis of diagnosis in about 20% of patients.

headline.text: The team recommends auditing recording completeness for stage, drug treatment, and multidisciplinary meetings, tracking access times using THL 21/2016 definitions, and standardising referrals with a named diagnostic contact.

details.text: Given Keski-Pohjanmaa's crude multidisciplinary team recording share of 1.4% (95% CI 0.4–4.8; n=2/148) versus 6.0% (893/14873) nationally and 48% missing stage nationally, the team recommends publishing county recording completeness for stage, drug treatment, and multidisciplinary coding, aligning with the STM roadmap's measure 3.2.1 plan for a quality registry decree by 2026–2028 and 90% coverage by 2029–2031.

Because the Health Care Act sets no maximum time for a cancer suspicion and national monitoring is lacking, the team recommends reporting access times and flagging stalled handovers using THL Ohjaus 21/2016 definitions for 16 cancers, while the STM roadmap's measure 3.1.2 plans national pathway descriptions and access times by 2026–2028 and for all significant cancers by 2029–2031.

The team recommends adopting a referral template and referring persistent symptoms after a normal X-ray, as set out in the KYS regional pathway document, since a mentor insight notes weak referrals get lower urgency ratings and the Filha programme's diagnostics recommendation with referral criteria and time limits is to be carried out before the 2030 mid-term evaluation.

Because no reviewed regional pathway document names a diagnostic-phase contact person, the team recommends naming a contact from referral to diagnosis, alongside the STM roadmap's measure 2.5.2 plan for standardised referral criteria and symptom-based models by 2026–2028 and measure 1.2.3 plan for named care-coordinator guidance by 2026–2028 and county adoption by 2029–2031.

q:4e702a20fe.claim_text: Finland has no unified national system to steer the drafting of cancer-specific treatment recommendations, or the implementation and monitoring of care pathways based on them (quality and effectiveness targets/indicators, including access to care, and cancer-specific and generic PROMs). Existing recommendations and pathways, and the targets and indicators to be monitored, are not coordinated nationally. This maintains regional inequality in the availability and effectiveness of cancer care.
q:4e702a20fe.quote: Suomessa ei ole yhtenäistä kansallista järjestelmää, joka ohjaisi syöpäkohtaisten hoitosuositusten laatimista sekä niihin perustuvien hoitoketjujen toteutusta ja seurantaa (laatu- ja vaikuttavuustavoitteet/indikaattorit, mukaan lukien hoitoonpääsy sekä syöpäkohtaiset ja geneeriset PROM-vointimittarit). Olemassa olevia hoitosuosituksia ja -ketjuja sekä seurattavia tavoitteita ja indikaattoreita ei koordinoida kansallisella tasolla. Tämä ylläpitää alueellista eriarvoisuutta syövän hoidon saatavuudessa ja vaikuttavuudessa.
q:4e702a20fe.quote_en: Finland does not have a uniform national system to guide the preparation of cancer-specific clinical guidelines and the implementation and monitoring of care pathways based on them (quality and effectiveness targets/indicators, including access to care as well as cancer-specific and generic PROM well-being measures). Existing clinical guidelines and care pathways as well as monitored targets and indicators are not coordinated at the national level. This maintains regional inequality in the availability and effectiveness of cancer care.

rec:1.claim_text: Team recommendation 1: Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts. Each wellbeing services county reports lung cancer access times (referral → first specialist visit → diagnosis → treatment start) using the definitions in THL's Hoitoonpääsyn seuranta syövän hoidossa (Ohjaus 21/2016). Until national target times exist, flag stalled handovers.
rec:1.location: §1. Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts

rec:2.claim_text: Team recommendation 2: A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact. Adopt a standard referral content list and template, modelled on KYS. • Add a rule for primary care: if symptoms persist after a normal X-ray, refer for a pulmonologist assessment. • Name a contact person for the diagnostic phase, from referral to diagnosis.
rec:2.location: §2. A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact
